examples.en: I looked around an old temple in Greece.

examples.ko: 언덕 위에 하얀 신전이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A white temple stands on the hill.

examples.ko: 이 신전은 이천 년 전에 지어졌어요.
examples.en: This temple was built two thousand years ago.
People made wishes in front of the temple.

examples.ko: 게임 속 신전에는 보물이 숨겨져 있어요.
examples.en: There is hidden treasure in the temple in the game.

examples.ko: 신전의 기둥이 아직도 튼튼하게 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The temple's pillars still stand strong.

explain: 신을 모시는 큰 건물을 말할 때 써요. 한국의 절은 '절', 교회는 '교회'라고 하고 '신전'은 그리스, 이집트처럼 고대 문명이나 판타지 게임에서 주로 나와요. 한국 전통 건물에는 거의 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 옛날 사람들은 신을 위해 큰 신전을 지었어요.
phrases.en: People in the old days built a big temple for their gods.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고대 이야기에서 '신전'과 가장 잘 어울리는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb that most naturally goes with 신전 in stories about ancient times.

phrases.en: I'll show you a photo of a Greek temple.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라 이름과 함께 써서 어느 문명의 신전인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with a country name to say which civilization's temple it is.

phrases.en: The temple's pillars are very tall.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여 신전의 일부를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 의 to talk about a part of the temple.

explain_en: Used for large buildings of ancient religions. Korean temples are called '절' and churches '교회'; '신전' appears for Greece, Egypt or fantasy games, and is rarely used for Korean traditional buildings.

t90.ax: A white temple stands on the hill.

examples.ko: 이 학교에는 작은 현악 앙상블이 있어요.
examples.en: This school has a small string ensemble.
The ensemble of piano and violin was truly beautiful.

examples.ko: 네 사람의 앙상블 덕분에 공연이 완벽했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the four people's ensemble, the performance was perfect.

examples.ko: 배우들의 앙상블 연기가 좋아서 영화가 재미있어요.
examples.en: The film is fun because the actors work so well together.
We practice every day to get in sync as an ensemble.

examples.ko: 공연이 끝나자 앙상블 단원들이 인사를 했어요.
examples.en: When the show ended, the ensemble members bowed.

explain: 음악에서는 여럿이 함께 연주하는 팀이나 그 호흡을 말하고, 영화나 연극에서는 배우들이 서로 잘 맞는 연기를 말해요. 프랑스어에서 온 외래어라서 '합주'나 '조화'로 바꿔 쓸 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: The two actors made a wonderful ensemble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여럿이 서로 잘 어울릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for when several people fit well together.

phrases.en: This team works together really well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호흡이 잘 맞는다는 칭찬으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment meaning the members are in good sync.

phrases.example: 우리 반은 오늘 합주 연습을 했어요.
phrases.en: Our class practiced playing together today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악에서 '앙상블'을 우리말로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A native-word replacement for 앙상블 in music.

explain_en: In music it means a group playing together or their sense of timing, and in film or theater it means actors who play well off each other. It is a loanword from French, and '합주' or '조화' can sometimes replace it.

t90.ax: This school has a small string ensemble.

en: to love; to like; to be fond of

examples.en: My grandfather is very fond of traditional tea.

examples.ko: 많은 사람이 이 브랜드의 제품을 애호해요.
examples.en: Many people love this brand's products.
I have been fond of classical music for a long time.
That writer is a novelist loved by readers.

examples.ko: 제가 애호하는 가게는 골목 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: The shop I love going to is at the end of the alley.

examples.ko: 저는 단 음식을 별로 애호하지 않아요.
examples.en: I'm not very fond of sweet food.

explain: '좋아하다'보다 격식 있고, 오랫동안 꾸준히 즐기고 아끼는 느낌이에요. 같은 취미를 즐기는 사람을 '애호가'라고 하는데, 이 말과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: He is a longtime jazz lover.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것을 오래 즐기고 아끼는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word for someone who has long enjoyed and cherished something.

phrases.example: 제가 애호하는 작가가 새 책을 냈어요.
phrases.en: A writer I love has published a new book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 모양이에요. 오래 아끼는 대상에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun, used for something one has cherished for a long time.

phrases.en: I like warm tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning and far more natural in daily conversation.

explain_en: It is more formal than '좋아하다' and suggests enjoying and cherishing something steadily over a long time. A person who enjoys a hobby this way is called an '애호가' (enthusiast), which is worth learning together.

dis.h: formal: love a hobby or interest

p.n: 사랑하다 is a stronger, more emotional love. 애호하다 means being a fond fan of something.

examples.en: An international expo was held in Yeosu.
The subway is crowded during the expo.
I looked at new books at a book expo.
I bought expo tickets in advance.
The theme of this expo is the environment.

examples.ko: 엑스포를 보러 외국인 관광객이 많이 와요.
examples.en: Many foreign tourists come to see the expo.

explain: 엑스포는 큰 국제 행사나 산업 전시 이름에 주로 붙고, 작은 행사에는 '박람회'나 '전시회'를 많이 써요. '대전 엑스포', '푸드 엑스포'처럼 이름 뒤에 붙는 경우도 흔해요.

phrases.en: This year our city is holding an expo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 여는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the organizer holding the event.

phrases.en: I will go to the expo with my family on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구경하러 가는 사람의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: What a visitor would say.

phrases.example: 엑스포 개막 날에는 사람이 정말 많았어요.
phrases.en: On the opening day of the expo, there were so many people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 시작되는 때를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time the event starts.

explain_en: 엑스포 mostly appears in the names of large international events or industry shows, while smaller events are usually called 박람회 or 전시회. It is also common as a name tag, as in 대전 엑스포 or 푸드 엑스포.

examples.en: That director is very famous in the film world.
The film industry is going through hard times these days.
I'm studying acting to get into the film world.
People from the film world gathered at the awards ceremony.
Young directors in the film world are getting attention.
He left the film world and became a novelist.

explain: '-계'는 어떤 분야의 사람들과 세계를 묶어 부르는 말이에요. '연예계', '정치계', '학계'처럼 쓰고, '영화계'는 감독, 배우, 제작사까지 영화와 관련된 사람들 전체를 말해요.

phrases.en: I saw news about the film world on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화 분야의 소식을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for news about the film field.

phrases.en: People from the film world gathered at the awards ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감독, 배우 같은 영화 관련 사람들을 묶어 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Groups together directors, actors, and others in film.

phrases.en: After graduating, I entered the film industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화 분야에서 일을 시작한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means starting to work in the film field.

explain_en: '-계' groups the people and world of a field together, as in '연예계', '정치계' and '학계'. '영화계' covers everyone connected to film, including directors, actors and producers.

en: to be colorful; to be multicolored; to be many-hued

examples.en: Fireworks decorated the night sky in dazzling colors.
Brilliantly colored hanbok were hanging in the market.
The Christmas tree is so colorful it dazzles my eyes.
I walked through a field of multicolored flowers.
The stage lights changed into a rainbow of colors.
The autumn mountains are a blaze of color because of the leaves.

explain: 여러 가지 색이 화려하게 어우러진 모습에 써요. '알록달록'은 귀엽고 가벼운 느낌이고, '오색찬란'은 더 화려하고 멋진 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The Christmas streets are full of dazzling, many-colored lights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 화려한 색을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe splendid colors.

phrases.en: The mountain in autumn colors is truly splendid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풍경이 여러 색으로 화려할 때 해요체로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite style for scenery shining in many colors.

phrases.en: The child is holding a colorful umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오색찬란'보다 쉽고 귀엽고 가벼운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and lighter, with a cuter feel than the headword.

explain_en: It describes many colors blending in a splendid way. '알록달록' feels cute and light, while '오색찬란' feels more gorgeous and grand.

t90.ax: I walked through a field of multicolored flowers.

examples.en: Grandma keeps kimchi in an earthenware jar.
An onggi jar is a vessel that breathes.
I bought a small earthenware pot at the market.
Bowls made of earthenware are heavy but sturdy.

examples.ko: 옹기 마을에서 직접 항아리를 빚어 봤어요.
examples.en: I shaped a jar myself in the pottery village.
Earthenware jars are lined up on the jangdokdae.

explain: 된장, 간장, 김치를 담는 갈색 항아리가 대표적이에요. '도자기'는 높은 온도에서 구운 매끈한 그릇이고, '옹기'는 숨구멍이 있어서 발효 음식을 두기에 좋다고 해요.

phrases.en: Food keeps longer when stored in earthenware.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옹기로 만든 그릇을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A name for vessels made of onggi earthenware.

phrases.en: I stored the soybean paste in an earthenware jar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발효 음식을 보관할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for storing fermented foods.

phrases.en: Earthenware jars are lined up in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간장, 된장을 담는 큰 항아리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the large jars that hold soy sauce or soybean paste.

explain_en: The typical example is the brown jar for 된장, 간장 and 김치. 도자기 is smooth, high-fired ware, whereas 옹기 is porous and said to be good for fermented food.

t90.ax: An onggi jar is a vessel that breathes.

examples.en: The couple danced a waltz at their wedding.

examples.ko: 왈츠 음악이 나오자 사람들이 짝을 지었어요.
examples.en: When waltz music started, people paired up.

examples.ko: 왈츠 스텝이 어려워서 매일 연습하고 있어요.
examples.en: The waltz steps are hard, so I practice every day.
We turned slowly to an elegant waltz.
The first dance I learned was the waltz.
A slow waltz is playing on the radio.

explain: '왈츠'는 3박자 춤이라 '하나, 둘, 셋' 하고 세는 느낌으로 춰요. 동사는 '추다'를 쓰고 '왈츠를 추다'처럼 같이 말해요. '탱고', '블루스'처럼 서양 춤 이름은 대부분 외래어 그대로 써요.

phrases.en: We danced a waltz at the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 춤 이름에는 동사 '추다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Dance names take the verb 추다.

phrases.en: I'm learning the waltz these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 춤을 익히는 중이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are learning the dance.

phrases.en: This waltz piece is very smooth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 왈츠에 맞는 음악을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to music written for a waltz.

explain_en: The '왈츠' is in three beats, danced with a feel of counting one-two-three. The verb is '추다', as in '왈츠를 추다'. Western dance names such as '탱고' and '블루스' are mostly used as loanwords.

en: to enter into an organization; to join an organization

examples.en: I joined a choir when I was in college.

examples.ko: 동생은 축구 클럽에 입단하려고 연습 중이에요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is practicing to join a soccer club.

examples.ko: 연습생으로 입단한 지 벌써 삼 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It's already been three years since I joined as a trainee.

examples.ko: 신인 선수가 프로팀에 입단하면 계약금을 받기도 해요.
examples.en: When a rookie joins a pro team, he sometimes receives a signing bonus.

examples.ko: 어느 극단에 입단할지 아직 고민 중이에요.
examples.en: I'm still deciding which theater troupe to join.

examples.ko: 입단하기 전에 간단한 시험을 봐야 해요.
examples.en: You have to take a simple test before joining.

explain: '팀에 입단하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요. 회사에 들어가는 건 '입사하다', 학교는 '입학하다'라서 팀, 극단, 합창단 같은 곳에만 어울려요.

phrases.en: I want to join the baseball team too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어가고 싶은 바람을 말할 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to express a wish to join.

phrases.en: My younger sibling ended up joining the theater troupe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과적으로 들어가게 되었다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense that someone came to join as a result.

phrases.en: After joining, I practice every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어간 다음의 일을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to continue talking about what happens after joining.

explain_en: It takes the particle '에', as in '팀에 입단하다'. Joining a company is '입사하다' and a school is '입학하다', so this verb fits only places like teams, troupes and choirs.

examples.ko: 이 도서관은 장서가 오십만 권이 넘어요.
examples.en: This library has a collection of more than five hundred thousand books.
Most of my grandfather's book collection is made up of old books.
Shall we search the university library's holdings?

examples.ko: 그분은 평생 모은 장서 전부를 마을 도서관에 기증했어요.
examples.en: He donated his entire lifelong book collection to the town library.

examples.ko: 이 대학의 장서에는 희귀한 고서도 많아요.
examples.en: This university's collection also includes many rare old books.

examples.ko: 장서 점검 때문에 오늘은 도서관이 일찍 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: The library closes early today because of the book inventory check.

explain: 도서관이나 개인이 가지고 있는 책 전체를 가리켜요. '장서가 많다', '장서 수'처럼 쓰고, 책 한 권을 말할 때는 그냥 '책'이라고 해요. '소장 도서'와 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: This library has a rich collection of books.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가지고 있는 책의 수와 종류가 많다는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment that the number and variety of books held is large.

phrases.en: My grandfather donated his book collection to the university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개인이 모은 책 전체를 다른 곳에 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means giving one's whole book collection to another place.

phrases.en: I search the library's holdings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장서'와 비슷하게 갖고 있는 책을 말해요. 도서관 검색에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 장서, it means books held; often seen in library searches.

explain_en: It refers to the whole set of books held by a library or a person. People say '장서가 많다' or '장서 수', and for a single book you just say '책'. It is used much like '소장 도서' (books in a collection).

examples.en: My mother is preparing the food to put on the ancestral rites table.

examples.ko: 제사상이 너무 커서 상을 두 개 붙였어요.
examples.en: The ritual table was so big that we put two tables together.

examples.ko: 제사상은 집안마다 차리는 방법이 조금씩 달라요.
examples.en: How the ritual table is set differs a little from family to family.

examples.ko: 큰집에서 제사상을 차리고 모두 절을 했어요.
examples.en: At my uncle's house we set the ritual table and everyone bowed.
In front of the ritual table, the family members bow one by one.

examples.ko: 제사상까지 다 차리고 나니 밤이 되었어요.
examples.en: By the time we finished setting even the ritual table, it was night.

explain: 조상에게 제사를 지낼 때 음식을 차려 놓는 상이에요. '상을 차리다'처럼 '제사상을 차리다'라고 말해요. 설이나 추석 아침에 지내는 제사는 '차례'라고 해서 일반 '제사'와 구분하기도 해요.

phrases.en: We set the ritual table at Grandmother's house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상을 차리다'와 같은 말로, 제사 음식을 올려 놓는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 상을 차리다, it means laying out the food for the ritual.

phrases.en: We put fruit and rice cakes on the ritual table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 음식을 제사상에 놓는다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means placing certain food on the ritual table.
phrases.en_equiv: to put on the ritual table

phrases.example: 우리 집은 일 년에 두 번 제사를 지내요.
phrases.en: My family holds ancestral rites twice a year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제사상'과 함께 알아 두면 좋은, 제사를 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is the action of holding the rite, useful to learn with 제사상.

explain_en: It is the table where food is laid out when holding rites for ancestors. You say '제사상을 차리다', like '상을 차리다'. The rites held on the morning of Seollal or Chuseok are called '차례', which is sometimes distinguished from a regular '제사'.

en: to transmit; to re-broadcast; to diffuse

examples.en: The broadcasting station aired the final live.
This channel will broadcast tomorrow's game live.
I can hear the voice broadcasting soccer live on the radio.

examples.ko: 행사를 온라인으로 중계방송해서 많은 사람이 봤어요.
examples.en: They broadcast the event live online, so many people watched.

examples.ko: 비 때문에 중계방송할 수 없다는 공지가 떴어요.
examples.en: A notice appeared saying they could not broadcast live because of the rain.
The announcer who broadcast the Olympics live gave an interview.

explain: '방송하다'보다 구체적으로, 지금 벌어지는 일을 바로 전한다는 느낌이에요. 줄여서 '중계하다', 실시간이면 '생중계하다'라고 해요. 주로 스포츠와 큰 행사에 써요.

phrases.en: This channel broadcasts the final.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중계방송하다'의 줄임말이에요. 말할 때 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of '중계방송하다', more common in speech.

phrases.en: They will broadcast the concert live this evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실시간이라는 점을 더 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Puts more stress on it being real time.
phrases.en_equiv: to broadcast live in real time

phrases.en: The broadcaster is airing the game right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it's happening right now.

explain_en: It is more specific than 방송하다: it carries the feeling of sending out what is happening right now. It is shortened to 중계하다, and 생중계하다 when it is real-time. It is mostly used for sports and big events.

examples.ko: 그 작가의 이름은 출판계에서 익히 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: That author's name is well known in the publishing world.
I often hear that the publishing industry is struggling.
People from the publishing world gathered at the book fair.
This year's talk of the publishing world is this novel.

examples.ko: 출판계는 요즘 전자책 시장에 관심이 많아요.
examples.en: The publishing world is very interested in the e-book market these days.
After graduating, I want to enter the publishing world.

explain: '-계'는 그 분야에서 일하는 사람들과 분위기 전체를 가리켜요. '연예계', '정치계', '체육계'도 같은 식이에요. 한 회사를 말하는 '출판사'와는 달리 업계 전체를 말해요.

phrases.en: I worked in the publishing industry for ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 출판계와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 사업 분야라는 느낌이 조금 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 출판계, with a slightly stronger business feel.

phrases.en: My older sister works in the publishing world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about someone's job field.

phrases.en: I saw news about the publishing world on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 분야의 소식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for news from that field.

explain_en: The suffix '-계' refers to all the people and the overall scene of a field, as in '연예계', '정치계' and '체육계'. Unlike '출판사', which is one company, 출판계 means the whole industry.

examples.en: The drum is a typical percussion instrument.
I learned percussion when I was little.
The percussion sound in this piece is impressive.
In an orchestra, the percussion sits at the back.
Drums and gongs are also percussion instruments.
The percussionist came up on stage.

explain: 치거나 두드리거나 흔들어서 소리를 내는 악기를 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 현악기, 관악기와 함께 악기를 나누는 큰 갈래예요. 꽹과리, 북, 장구 같은 전통 악기도 타악기예요.

phrases.en: I heard a percussion performance at the show yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타악기'로 하는 연주를 말할 때 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about playing percussion instruments.

phrases.en: I play percussion every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두드려서 소리를 내는 악기라서 '치다'와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: '치다' (to hit) fits because these instruments are struck.

phrases.en: The percussion sound was so loud that my heart pounded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 타악기에서 나는 소리를 말할 때 '소리' 앞에 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before '소리' to refer to the sound made by percussion instruments.

explain_en: This groups instruments that make sound when struck, tapped or shaken. It is one of the main categories alongside string and wind instruments. Traditional instruments like the kkwaenggwari, buk and janggu are percussion too.

examples.en: In this performance, the pianist plays together with the orchestra.

examples.ko: 두 가수가 처음으로 협연한 무대가 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The stage where the two singers performed together for the first time became a hot topic.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 유명한 지휘자와 협연하고 싶었어요.
examples.en: Since I was young, I wanted to perform with a famous conductor.

examples.ko: 협연하는 동안 서로 눈빛을 맞추며 호흡을 확인했어요.
examples.en: While performing together, they made eye contact and checked their timing.

examples.ko: 그 두 사람은 이번 가을에 협연하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Those two decided to perform together this fall.
I'm so nervous because I'm going to perform together with my teacher.

explain: '오케스트라와 협연하다'처럼 '~와/과'와 함께 쓰는 일이 많아요. 클래식뿐 아니라 가수끼리 함께 무대에 설 때도 쓰고, 일상에서는 '같이 공연하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 두 가수가 이번 축제에서 같이 공연해요.
phrases.en: The two singers will perform together at this festival.
phrases.nuance_ko: '협연하다'와 비슷한 뜻으로, 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 협연하다 and easier to say in daily conversation.

phrases.en: He ended up performing with a famous orchestra.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게 되다'를 붙여 기회가 생겼다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-게 되다' it gives the sense that the chance came about.

phrases.en: I also want to perform with an orchestra someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여 바라는 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-고 싶다' it expresses a wish.

explain_en: It is often used with '~와/과', as in '오케스트라와 협연하다'. It is used not only in classical music but also when singers share a stage, and in daily life people also say '같이 공연하다'.
